scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: URGENT!! The other lab has DISAPPEARED for the whole
office!! All morning none of their machines answer any of our PCs --
everything else works, it's just the lab that's gone. Something that carries
us over to the lab must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at
the connection and get us back to their machines? We need them TODAY!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested end-to-end reachability from multiple office PCs (office_pc, enquiry, exam_cell, tpo) to multiple hosts in both labs (IT and CS). All probes succeeded with 0% loss and normal RTTs (~1–5 ms): e.g., office_pc -> it_lab1 (192.168.1.3), it_hod (192.168.1.2), cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3), cs_hod (192.168.2.2), cs_lab3 (192.168.2.5), and similar results from enquiry/exam_cell/tpo to it_lab2 (192.168.1.4) and cs_lab2 (192.168.2.4). Office also reaches the servers segment (office_pc -> pc1 at 1.0.0.5) successfully. This demonstrates the L3 interconnect and forwarding across router1 (office side) and router0 (lab side) via wan_r0_r1 are operating correctly, and the access switches and LAN interfaces are passing traffic.

Mechanism-wise, if a routing/link issue existed between office and the labs, ICMP would fail broadly, but we observe consistent bidirectional replies from diverse lab hosts. Localization therefore points to no fault on the inter-site path (router1 eth0 toward switch2; router1<->router0 WAN; router0 toward switch0/switch1).

Root cause: No current network fault found; the earlier report was likely transient or application-layer (e.g., service not listening, host firewall, or name-resolution issue) rather than transport/connectivity.

Corrective fix: None required at the network layer. Please re-test the required application from office. If issues persist, verify the target lab service is running/listening on the expected port and that DNS/hostnames resolve; also check host firewalls on the lab machines.
